segments.he: אִם הָיָה דְבַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת – חַיָּיב לְשַׁלֵּם. מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ: לֹא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת מַמָּשׁ, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ פָּרָה וְחוֹרֵשׁ בָּהּ, חֲמוֹר וּמְחַמֵּר אַחֲרָיו – חַיָּיבִין לְהַחֲזִיר, מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד אֲבִיהֶן.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches, with regard to one who left a stolen item to his children, «if» the item «was something that may serve» as a legal «guarantee» of a loan, the heirs «are obligated to pay» the owner. The Gemara states that «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi would «teach» this mishna to «Rabbi Shimon, his son,» and explain that it does «not» refer only to «something that can actually» serve as «a guarantee» for a loan, i.e., land. «Rather,» it refers «even» to «a cow» that «he plows with,» or «a donkey» that «he drives» by directing it from «behind,» which the heirs «are obligated to return because of the honor of their father,» so that people will not continually point out that the inheritance was stolen and thereby disgrace their deceased parent.
